title: Arithmetico-Geometric and Harmonic Progressions
tagline: Year 3 — AGP series, harmonic progressions, and the relation between AM, GM and HM

introduction.overview: Besides AP and GP there are two more progression types that appear in aptitude tests. A harmonic progression (HP) is a sequence whose reciprocals form an AP. An arithmetico-geometric progression (AGP) multiplies the terms of an AP by the terms of a GP. This chapter also covers the relation AM ≥ GM ≥ HM and its use in maximum and minimum questions.
introduction.placementRelevance: HP and the AM-GM-HM relation are asked directly in company aptitude and logic papers; AGP appears in advanced sections.
introduction.realWorldContext: Average speed over equal distances is a harmonic mean, which links this chapter to time-and-distance problems.

learningObjectives: Recognise an HP and find its terms
Use AM, GM and HM for two numbers
Remember AM × HM = GM² for two numbers
Apply the inequality AM ≥ GM ≥ HM

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: AP: constant difference. GP: constant ratio. HP: reciprocals form an AP.

coreDefinitions: Harmonic mean of x and y: HM = 2xy/(x + y).
Arithmetic mean AM = (x + y)/2 and geometric mean GM = √(xy).
For positive unequal numbers, AM > GM > HM, and GM² = AM × HM.
AGP: terms of the form (a + (n − 1)d) rⁿ⁻¹.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: HM gives more weight to smaller numbers because it averages reciprocals. That is why the average speed for equal distances at 40 and 60 km/h is the harmonic mean, 48 km/h, not 50.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: For any HP question, flip every term to get an AP, do the AP work, then flip back.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: HP term
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Tₙ = 1/(a + (n − 1)d) where a, d belong to the reciprocal AP

mainNarrative: If 1/2, 1/4, 1/6, … is an HP then 2, 4, 6, … is its AP of reciprocals. The 5th term is the reciprocal of the 5th term of 2, 4, 6, …, which is 10, so T₅ = 1/10.
To insert a harmonic mean between 40 and 60, compute 2 × 40 × 60/(40 + 60) = 48. That is also the average speed of a trip with equal distances at 40 and 60 km/h.
For two numbers AM × HM = GM². With 40 and 60: 50 × 48 = 2400 = 40 × 60.
A simple AGP: 1 + 2x + 3x² + …, for |x| < 1, sums to 1/(1 − x)². At x = 1/2 the sum is 4.
The relation AM ≥ GM ≥ HM holds for any positive numbers, with equality only when all the numbers are equal.

deepDiveAspects.title: Three terms in HP
deepDiveAspects.content: If a, b, c are in HP then b = 2ac/(a + c) and 1/b is the mean of 1/a and 1/c.

deepDiveAspects.title: Average speed
deepDiveAspects.content: For equal distances the average speed is the harmonic mean; for equal times it is the arithmetic mean.

solvedExamples.title: Harmonic mean
solvedExamples.question: A car goes from A to B at 40 km/h and returns at 60 km/h. Find its average speed.
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Total time is longer at the lower speed, so the average is below 50.

solvedExamples.title: AM, GM, HM
solvedExamples.question: The AM of two numbers is 25 and their GM is 15. Find their HM.
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Check the order AM > GM > HM: 25 > 15 > 9.

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Reciprocate an HP to an AP; use GM² = AM × HM for two numbers.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using AP formulas on an HP

commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Use the harmonic mean for equal distances.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: AM > GM > HM, so the answer must fit between the means.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: GM² = AM × HM is a quick check.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: HP ties to speed and work problems.
